title: Crypto CTF Misc
html:
Crypto CTF Misc

This section collects techniques that appear in cryptography challenges but do not fit neatly into the other categories.

Esoteric languages

Technique

Use this workflow when a challenge requires running an esoteric-language program and decoding its output.

If a challenge gives you code that does not look like a standard language:

  • Identify the language by searching for a distinctive token or instruction sequence.
  • Use an online interpreter or a Docker image.
  • If the output is weird, look for layered encoding/compression after execution.

A useful language index is the Esolang wiki.[1] For ordinary encoding and compression layers, use the Crypto CTF workflow. If the clue is invisible text rather than executable syntax, check text steganography.

Exfiltrating preloaded interpreter state

If a challenge accepts esoteric-language source and runs it in a custom interpreter, inspect its initial memory, stack and output instructions before treating the source as a decoding puzzle. When the interpreter preloads a secret onto a Befunge stack, a short program can pop and print the existing bytes without computing them. This requires control of the executed source and an output opcode; it does not work against a normal empty interpreter. In a Befunge challenge, the input below repeatedly emitted characters from a flag preloaded in reverse order on the stack.[2][3]

>,<

> starts execution to the right, , pops and prints a character, and < sends the instruction pointer back to ,. Check the custom interpreter's underflow and instruction-limit behavior: the cited implementation stops when the stack is exhausted or after 1,024 instructions. If the secret is not directly on the stack, inspect other initialized state and available output/read instructions instead of assuming standard Befunge semantics.[3][4]

References

  • [1] Esolang, the esoteric programming languages wiki
  • [2] WolvCTF 2024 Befuddled1 original writeup
  • [3] WolvCTF 2024 Befuddled1 interpreter source
  • [4] Befunge language reference
